mi-sbe-2026-collins-terence.name: Terence Collins
mi-sbe-2026-collins-terence.bio: Senior financial analyst with a Detroit automaker and former Grosse Pointe Public Schools board member (2023-2024).

positions.stance: "We must ensure parents have a strong voice in their children's education decisions."
"We must demand that every dollar spent on education is spent wisely and improves outcomes for all students."
Says he will "return the focus to reading, writing, and math while ensuring that every tax dollar is spent wisely."

mi-sbe-2026-moeggenberg-bree.name: Bree Moeggenberg
mi-sbe-2026-moeggenberg-bree.bio: Licensed childcare provider and business owner, and former State Committee member.

positions.stance: Calls to restore classroom stability and neutrality: "Politics must get out," address behavior disruptions, and consider smaller class sizes and added recess.
Wants curriculum revived to include critical thinking at every grade level, with a focus on outcomes rather than compliance, plus life and civic skills.
"We don't need more money to increase student success, we need more useful spending that provides for resources where they are needed most."

mi-um-regent-2026-brown-paul.name: Paul Brown
mi-um-regent-2026-brown-paul.bio: University of Michigan Regent since 2018; attorney and former Michigan Economic Development Corporation vice president who taught finance at U-M's College of Engineering.

positions.stance: Says he grew the Go Blue Guarantee, making U-M tuition-free for Michigan families earning up to $125,000 per year.
Says his work helped grow enrollment of students of color by more than 150% to over 40% of the student body.
Describes himself as the "Union Regent" and cites passing a pro-union organizing policy and doubling the number of campus unions.
Says he established a "sanctuary campus" by prohibiting ICE from accessing campus-controlled property and refused to release transgender patients' records to the Trump administration.
Wants U-M to act as an economic engine for Michigan and says he committed the university to campus-wide carbon neutrality.

mi-um-regent-2026-makled-amir.name: Amir Makled
mi-um-regent-2026-makled-amir.bio: Civil rights attorney and University of Michigan-Dearborn graduate.

positions.stance: "A top public university must be accessible to everyone"; every campus and student deserves equal respect, resources and representation.
"Higher education should open doors, not create lifelong debt"; committed to affordability across the Ann Arbor, Dearborn and Flint campuses.
Defends free speech and academic freedom, including students' and faculty's right to speak out against injustice "without fear of retaliation or surveillance."
Will push for ethical governance, responsible decision-making, and "an end to intimidation tactics that undermine the university's public mission."
Supports fair treatment and dignity for faculty, staff and healthcare workers across the University of Michigan system.

mi-um-regent-2026-epstein-lena.name: Lena Epstein
mi-um-regent-2026-epstein-lena.bio: Co-owner, board member and executive of Vesco Oil Corporation.

positions.stance: Hold the line on tuition through disciplined budgeting, bring down student housing costs, and expand need-based aid.
Open more seats for in-state students and build pathways from Michigan high schools and community colleges into U-M.
Demand transparency in spending and real oversight of university leadership, and "root out waste and fraud."
Committed to ensuring "activism never crosses into harassment" and that Jewish students are never intimidated or marginalized.
Supports expanding research collaborations with Israel and strongly opposes BDS divestment campaigns involving the university's endowment.

mi-um-regent-2026-schostak-michael.name: Michael Schostak
mi-um-regent-2026-schostak-michael.bio: Bloomfield Township Treasurer and former finance lecturer at Wayne State University's Ilitch School of Business.

positions.stance: "I'll push for more undergraduates to be Michigan residents," noting half of U-M students come from outside Michigan.
Wants expanded Go Blue Guarantee income thresholds, home equity and small-business assets removed from aid formulas, and the endowment used to lower costs.
"No student or faculty member should fear for their safety, property, or academic standing because of their beliefs"; wants consistent enforcement of speech rules.
Says the Regents must take an active role in expanding student housing supply so Ann Arbor remains accessible for Michigan families.
Will demand transparency and accountability in U-M's budget: "No more $12 million dollar investigations with hidden results."

mi-msu-trustee-2026-scott-brianna.name: Brianna Scott
mi-msu-trustee-2026-scott-brianna.bio: Muskegon attorney and law-firm founder, former assistant prosecutor, and MSU Board of Trustees member since 2018.

positions.stance: "Restoring trust in MSU through disciplined leadership, transparency, and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars."
"Building a campus where every Spartan feels safe, supported, and empowered to succeed."
Keeping "a world-class education accessible while investing in the full student experience—from enrollment to career readiness."
Strengthening MSU through "research excellence, workforce readiness, and support for labor and economic growth."

mi-msu-trustee-2026-zemke-kelly.name: Kelly Tebay Zemke
mi-msu-trustee-2026-zemke-kelly.bio: MSU Trustee since 2019 and past board chair; works in government and external relations for a museum.

positions.stance: Expand Spartan Advantage, MSU's free-tuition program, "even further to give more future Spartan Michiganders affordable access to MSU."
Build on the free-tuition effort to include room and board programs so every Spartan has access to an affordable higher education.
"Break down all barriers to student success before they arrive on campus, while they're there, and after they leave."
Expand cost-free student health services at MSU's campus health center toward a "'wherever, whenever' possibility for all students."

mi-msu-trustee-2026-maday-julie.name: Julie Maday
mi-msu-trustee-2026-maday-julie.bio: Former Novi City Councilwoman and Planning Commission member; current member of Novi's Economic Development Committee.

positions.stance: Pledges to re-introduce "a culture of accountability and transparency" and restore a common-sense approach to the Board focused on students rather than politics.
Will support the foundation of Title IX and "reject the idea that men should be allowed to compete in women's sports."
Pledges to embrace diversity of thought and reject cancel culture, citing the First Amendment right to freedom of speech.
"Universities were created to teach students how to think, not what to think"; will stand up for conservative voices on campus.
Would be "a voice of rationality, with an emphasis on critical thought and practical solutions," citing extended COVID-era restrictions at MSU.

mi-msu-trustee-2026-victory-roger.name: Roger Victory
mi-msu-trustee-2026-victory-roger.bio: Fourth-generation farmer and owner of Victory Farms; Michigan State Senator and former State Representative.

positions.stance: "Support strong academic programs, faculty excellence, and degrees that prepare students for real-world careers."
"Champion MSU's leadership in agriculture, food systems, and Extension programs that serve farmers, families, and communities statewide."
"Promote responsible governance that respects taxpayers, students, and families while protecting MSU's long-term strength."
"Ensure the Board of Trustees operates with integrity, clarity, and a focus on MSU's mission—not politics."

mi-wsu-governor-2026-akeel-shereef.name: Shereef Akeel
mi-wsu-governor-2026-akeel-shereef.bio: Civil rights and human rights attorney who runs a law firm in Oakland County; holds an M.B.A. and CPA.

positions.stance: "Champion affordable tuition and debt reduction" and fight for increased state funding to keep higher education within reach for working families.
Expand financial aid and scholarships, prioritizing first-generation, low-income and nontraditional students.
Invest in open educational resources and encourage faculty to adopt low-cost materials to reduce textbook expenses.
"Advocate for stronger faculty retention through competitive salaries and modern infrastructure."
Says partnerships with Detroit industries will create internships and job pipelines for graduates.

mi-wsu-governor-2026-mack-richard.name: Richard Mack
mi-wsu-governor-2026-mack-richard.bio: Union-side labor and civil rights attorney for 28 years.

positions.stance: Wants to "help deliver a top-notch education for students, while fairly compensating the faculty and staff who make that education possible."
Wants to "expand the University's reach into the community, both in the city of Detroit and across the state."
"I am driven to help make WSU more affordable, safe, and connected to the entire state of Michigan."

mi-wsu-governor-2026-anuzis-andy.name: Andy Anuzis
mi-wsu-governor-2026-anuzis-andy.bio: Principal of Cornerstone Lincoln-King High School in Detroit and former president of the Cornerstone Schools network; former chief of staff in the Michigan House and U.S. Congress.

positions.stance: "Top priorities are affordability, preparing students for successful careers, and developing a generation of intellectually cultivated citizens."
Would scrutinize ancillary projects and departments each budget cycle to free resources for teaching and research and keep tuition affordable.
Says research, teaching and workforce preparation are all critical, but "excellence in teaching and learning is of paramount importance."
Says hiring and firing a president "should not be based on a board member's personal or ideological dispositions" but on advancing the university's mission.
Would encourage Wayne State to sign the Chicago Statement on free expression and explore creating a Wayne State Civil Society Institute.

mi-wsu-governor-2026-murphy-christa.name: Christa Murphy
mi-wsu-governor-2026-murphy-christa.bio: Wayne State alumna and technology executive at Meta, Samsung and GM; 16-year credit union board member.

positions.stance: Will push for "rigorous budget discipline," regular program reviews favoring degrees with strong employment outcomes, and sunsetting offerings that don't serve students.
Will push for "deeper partnerships with Detroit's business and civic communities to ensure graduates are career-ready."
Will champion student support programs, co-op and internship pipelines into high-wage careers, and completion initiatives.

al-sc7-2026-mendheim-brad.name: Brad Mendheim
al-sc7-2026-mendheim-brad.bio: Associate Justice of the Alabama Supreme Court since 2018; former circuit and district judge and assistant district attorney in Houston and Henry Counties.

al-sc8-2026-dunham-ashleigh.name: Ashleigh Meyer Dunham
al-sc8-2026-dunham-ashleigh.bio: Referee in Jefferson County Juvenile Court and fertility attorney at Magic City Fertility Law.

positions.stance: Believes "the role of a justice is not to impose personal views, but to faithfully interpret the law and apply it to the facts."
Pledges "a deep respect for the Alabama and United States Constitutions" and "a commitment to considering the real-world impact of every ruling."

al-sc8-2026-shaw-greg.name: Greg Shaw
al-sc8-2026-shaw-greg.bio: Senior Associate Justice of the Alabama Supreme Court; former Court of Criminal Appeals judge and Supreme Court staff attorney.

positions.stance: "A judge's job is not to make policy"; says a justice should read the text of a law, respect precedent faithful to the text, and leave lawmaking to the people.
Describes himself as a constitutional conservative who "will always apply the law as it is written."
"Conservative judging means enforcing the criminal laws as written, while respecting the rights of the accused."

nm-coa-pos1-2026-houghton-kris.name: Kris Houghton
nm-coa-pos1-2026-houghton-kris.bio: Judge of the New Mexico Court of Appeals since 2025; former Assistant U.S. Attorney in Albuquerque.

mi-sbe-2026-charafeddine-wissam.name: Wissam Charafeddine
mi-sbe-2026-charafeddine-wissam.bio: Engineer, educator and author from Dearborn who works as a Family & Community Engagement Liaison in Michigan schools.

positions.stance: Commits to a district-by-district CS implementation transparency report, a CS teacher pipeline for the 2027 mandate, and STEAM integration across all subjects.
Calls for mandatory Michigan ed-tech quality standards before purchase, teacher review panels in procurement, and an annual public ed-tech transparency report.
Supports a funded culturally competent family engagement pilot, a mandatory language access standard, and state funding for family engagement coordinators.
